pageSections.title: A grounded answer needs a traceable source path
pageSections.description: The system must record the selected documents, retrieved passages, prompt, model output, and evaluation result for each consequential research interaction.
pageSections.context: Refract implements these controls for paper questions, cross-paper synthesis, and active-recall grading.

pageSections.title: Keep the source visible while the model responds
pageSections.description: The Reader places the PDF, selected passage, and assistant response in one workspace and saves the paper and page reference with the evidence.
pageSections.caption: Passage-grounded question generation inside the Refract Reader.

pageSections.title: Four records make an LLM result reviewable

items.label: Scope
items.title: Selected source set
items.body: Record the papers and research question supplied to retrieval or synthesis.

items.label: Evidence
items.title: Passage and page references
items.body: Store the exact excerpts used for the answer and keep their document identifiers.

items.label: Generation
items.title: Prompt and model version
items.body: Retain the instructions, model name, structured schema, and generated result.

items.label: Evaluation
items.title: Rubric and reviewer output
items.body: Record dimension scores, rubric hits, omissions, feedback, and any sampled human grade.

pageSections.title: The source set constrains the answer before generation
pageSections.description: A session identifies the active papers and question before document chunks enter retrieval.
pageSections.markdown:
Refract indexes document chunks in ChromaDB and keeps paper records in PostgreSQL. Reader questions begin from the active document or selected passage. Compare begins from a chosen paper set and research question.

These inputs define the material available to the model and allow the final output to list its coverage. Missing evidence becomes visible as missing coverage instead of being hidden inside fluent prose.

pageSections.title: Structured grading separates three kinds of error
pageSections.description: Free-recall answers are scored on the core claim, reference details, and faithfulness to the source.
pageSections.markdown:
The grader returns structured fields for rubric hits, missing points, corrective feedback, and dimension scores. Refract also records the learner's confidence before source reveal.

Human-grade export supports inter-rater checks on a sample of attempts. Model name, prompt version, reveal mode, and source reference remain attached to each row so disagreements can be investigated.

pageSections.title: A model change should pass the same recorded cases

items.title: Freeze the case inputs
items.body: Keep the research question, selected sources, expected points, and rubric version stable.

items.title: Run the candidate
items.body: Record the model, prompt, retrieved passages, structured output, and latency.

items.title: Compare dimensions
items.body: Measure core-claim coverage, reference-detail coverage, faithfulness, and reviewer agreement separately.

items.title: Inspect failures
items.body: Review unsupported statements, missed evidence, retrieval gaps, and rubric disagreement by category.

items.title: Release with a bounded claim
items.body: Describe the tested cases, observed result, and untested populations or workflows.

pageSections.title: Refract implements the measurement path
pageSections.description: The repository contains passage references, structured recall grading, version fields, FSRS state, and human-grade export.
pageSections.markdown: Those records support technical evaluation of model behavior. Claims about improved retention or scientific decision quality require a completed user study with a registered protocol, comparison condition, and analyzed outcomes.
